newsitem.title: USA: Whitman to spin off Midas, Hussmann.
newsitem.headline: Whitman to spin off Midas, Hussmann.

text.p: Midas International, the world's largest automotive service franchise, will be spun off as an independently traded company so its parent, Whitman Corp., can focus on its giant Pepsi-Cola bottling business, Whitman said Monday.
It said it will also spin off Hussmann Corp., a major food refrigeration systems maker, as part of the plan to shift direct ownership of the subsidiaries to Whitman shareholders.
Whitman owns Pepsi-Cola General Bottlers, the world's largest independent Pepsi-Cola franchisee, which accounts for half of the company's sales and more than half of its operating income.
Whitman said its board also authorised the repurchase of an additional five million shares of its common stock.
Analysts applauded the announcement, boosting Whitman's stock $2.50 to $25.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in late-morning trading.

Whitman said the spin-offs are subject to a ruling by the Internal Revenue Service that the transactions would be non-taxable to the Rolling Meadows, Ill.-based company and its shareholders, as well as market conditions at the time.

The company said it is likely to take some special charges later this year, although it has yet to determine the size or timing. The charges will be to facilitate the spin-offs and position the companies for future growth, it added.
"We believe that as independent publicly traded companies, our businesses will realise a number of benefits," Whitman Chairman Bruce Chelberg said in a statement.

"They'll be better able to attract and retain key management personnel, achieve further improvements in productivity and efficiency, realise new business opportunities and win new customers for their products and services."
Hussmann is the world's largest supplier of refrigeration systems for the food industry, with operations in nine countries. Sales were more than $1.0 billion in 1996.
Midas is the world's largest franchised automotive service operation, with more than 2,500 stores in 17 countries. Worldwide retail sales by Midas dealers were more than $1.3 billion in 1996.

Whitman said it expects second-quarter earnings per share to be 5 cents to 7 cents below the 39 cents reported in the year-ago period, due to the weak performance of Midas and Pepsi-Cola General Bottlers.
Whitman said Pepsi-Cola General Bottlers was hurt by unusually competitive pricing and unseasonably cold weather, as well as a $3.0 million charge for staff cuts.
Midas faced soft consumer demand for automotive repair and a less favourable mix of products and services, it said.
Whitman said it expects to maintain its strong capital structure and investment grade credit after the spin-offs, which it hopes to complete in six to nine months.
"We expect Whitman will continue to have considerable financial flexibility to take advantage of the significant growth opportunities which exist in the beverage industry," Chelberg said.

Whitman said it will use repurchased shares for general corporate purposes, including its employee benefit and long-term incentive programmes. Shares will be bought back from time to time through open market and privately negotiated transactions.
The company has repurchased about 9.5 million share in the past four years out of a total of 10.5 milion shares that have been previously authorised for repurchase.
